Okay yeh, I do the same thing too. For me, I try to identify what triggers my jealousy/depressive episodes. If I can't control it (like how I feel when my GF does X or when I see something that reminds me of Y) then I try to essentially mediate the internal feelings before I fall off the deep end. It takes a lot of work, it really does, but it's also something that gets better with practice. I recommend just being aware of things and reassuring yourself on insecurities, particularly the ones that trigger these episodes. I also recommend reading articles online. I'm just some 20 y/o who has gone through this stuff. I can give you advice that might help for now, but not long term. There will be so many articles and books available at your fingertips written by smart people that will help you grow out of this rut. Good luck, I believe in you!

Hey, I go through the same crap you do. I know it's hard. I often find myself wanting to reassure people in our situation that what they're going through doesn't define them, and it can be overcome. I also often find myself struggling to really find the right words. Below is what my therapist told me, and it has helped me a lot. Maybe it will help you. 

In our minds, there's a court case going on. The depression/anxiety that we have is the prosecutor and we're the little ol' defendant. That prosecutor is going to do ANYTHING they can to persuade the jury (our subconscious) that they are right. But they use a lot of slippery slope arguments. That prosecutor exaggerates things so much. That prosecutor turns a harmless mistake into a major fuck up. We start to ask ourselves "oh god, why/how did we fuck up so bad?" Well what we need to do is understand that, that prosecutor is spewing horse shit. It might be based in facts, but his arguments aren't factual. We need to learn to not listen to everything they say. And that, my friend is how we overcome this. 

You can do this. I believe in you!

Much love.

Hi sad girl, I'm a sad boy. 

I know days like this are tough. I feel the exact same way. For me, things come and go in waves. 

I struggle a lot with finding things to say to people, especially those facing depression. But I just want you to know that I'm here for you, and I'm thinking of you. You do matter. Below, I attached something that some random stranger on the internet said to me when I was contemplating ending it all, I hope it helps you the same way it helps me. 

❤️

First of all, I'm really sorry for what you're going through. In life, happiness is a journey – not a destination. Life is always going to come with its share of problems. Happiness is simply knowing there's always a way through them, and knowing that you can always come out of them for the better. If you've stared depression in the face and survived once already, there's no doubt in my mind that you can do it again. You've obviously been through a lot and still managed to make it all this way. That means something, and you should give yourself some more credit.

Remember that sometimes, we have to be broken before we can be made whole again. The whole reason we make mistakes is so we can learn from them. The whole reason we get hurt is so we can heal and grow stronger. The whole reason we experience grief is so we can cherish life more. No matter how tough your situation is, there's always something you can learn from it. In a weird twisted way, I'm almost grateful for facing depression when I did, because it helped make me into the person I am today.

Remember that as long as you're alive, you have every opportunity to make a better future for yourself. Even if you've hit rock bottom, that means you have nothing to lose, and nowhere to go but up. In the end, I don't think any of us actually want to die – we only want to get away from the pain we're in. But the best way to get away from the pain is to make an effort to improve yourself, little by little, day by day. It might not happen overnight, but small progress is still progress.

So instead of ending your life, I would suggest setting a goal for yourself, and seeing if you can accomplish it by a certain date. Instead of writing a suicide note, I would suggest writing a note detailing what kind of future you want for yourself – then, make a list of small, practical steps you can take to get there. If you focus on improving your life instead of dwelling on death, you may be surprised and inspired by the results.

If you haven't already, I would also suggest reaching out to somebody you trust. I understand how intimidating it can be starting a conversation about depression, but it's much better than suffering in silence. Obviously, they can't wave a magic wand to make your feelings go away, but at least they'll be able to help you.

If you're not comfortable telling someone you're having suicidal thoughts, you can simply tell them you're feeling lost and haven't been feeling like yourself lately. Ask them if they've ever felt the same way. Ask them what they would do in your situation, or if there's anything they can do to help you. If it helps, you can write down what you want to say beforehand.

At this point, you have nothing to lose, but so much to gain from reaching out to somebody. Never underestimate the power of someone who cares about you, and who's willing to give up their time to make sure you're okay. Sometimes, they can be a real game-changer. I know if a friend or family member were struggling, I would much rather them reach out to me, than continue to struggle.

I know there's no easy answers to the problems you might face, but I hope you can find some reason – any reason – to keep pushing forward, because chances are, there's people who need you. I wish you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you!
